titulo: Video is code: a composition with time and deterministic render
lead: In motion graphics as code, the video is a page that knows how to draw any instant. A headless browser asks for frame 0, then 1, then 2, and FFmpeg stitches them into an MP4. If the same input always gives the same frames, you can redo, fix, and version the video like code. In this lesson you prove it on your own machine.
objetivo: prove on your own machine that the same composition gives the same frames, and find what breaks that.

aprende.t: The four pieces: composition, clock, headless browser, and encoder
Compare two renders frame by frame with one command
Why Math.random and Date.now break the video
Seeded random: variety without losing repeatability

hero_alt: A film strip on a cold light table, with a white circle that grows from frame to frame.

secoes.sub: Tap each piece. HyperFrames (HTML) and Remotion (React) follow the same design.

nos.detalhe: A file that describes what is on screen and how it changes over time. In HyperFrames it is an index.html with data-* attributes; in Remotion, a React component. It is text: it fits in git and the agent edits it.
The engine doesn't let the animation run on its own: it asks for an exact instant (2.5 s, or frame 75 at 30 fps) and the composition draws that instant. That's why you can jump to any point.
A windowless Chrome opens the composition, goes to the requested instant, and takes a picture of the frame. On first use HyperFrames downloads this browser (about 240 MB as of 10/19/2026).
FFmpeg stitches the photos together in order and writes the MP4 (H.264). If the photos are the same, so is the final file.

secoes.legenda: Deterministic = run it twice in the same environment and get the same frames. That's what lets you fix one detail without redoing the rest.
secoes.dica: Across different machines, GPU and fonts can change a few pixels; to repeat it on another machine, the 0.8.176 render has --docker ("deterministic render") and --no-browser-gpu.

secoes.sub: Three sources of chance that the HyperFrames lint looks for.

texto: Each render draws again: the same 12 points show up in different places.
The fix is a seeded draw (mulberry32): the same seed gives the same numbers, every time.

exemplo.texto: const sorteio = mulberry32(42); then sorteio() in place of Math.random().

texto: The current time changes with every render and every frame.
Everything that animates has to come from the time the engine provides, never from the computer's clock.
Fetching data from the internet during the render can bring back a different answer or fail midway.
Fetch it beforehand, save it to a file in the folder, and read it from there (lesson 7 does this with the captions).

secoes.titulo: The test run: two renders, compared frame by frame
secoes.sub: Two nearly identical compositions: one uses Math.random, the other a seeded draw. Each one is rendered twice and compared by the hash of each frame.

blocos.rot: Terminal · two renders of each and the comparison
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-motion-v72/kit
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-motion/a1; rm -rf "$E"; mkdir -p "$E"
for ex in a1-sorteio a1-semente; do
  cp -r "$K/exemplos/$ex" "$E/$ex"; cd "$E/$ex"
  for n in 1 2; do
    npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 render --quality draft --workers 1 --quiet --output "render-$n.mp4" > /dev/null 2>&1
  done
  echo "## $ex"; bash "$K/comparar-quadros.sh" render-1.mp4 render-2.mp4; echo "saída: $?"
done

abas.html:
## a1-sorteio
DIFEREM: 89 de 90 quadros
saída: 1
## a1-semente
IGUAIS: 90/90 quadros
saída: 0

That's 90 frames (3 s at 30 fps). With Math.random only the first one matches; with the seed, all 90 do. The first render downloads hyperframes@0.8.176 and the browser, so it takes longer.

abas.rot: Common mistake: comparing the whole file
abas.html: Comparing the MP4 with md5sum can come out different even when the frames are the same (file metadata). The comparar-quadros.sh script decodes the file and compares the image of each frame with ffmpeg -f framemd5.

secoes.titulo: The lint finds the chance before the render
secoes.sub: The same pair of compositions run through the HyperFrames lint. It points to the line and suggests the seed.

blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-motion-v72/kit
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 NO_COLOR=1
for ex in a1-sorteio a1-semente; do
  cd "$K/exemplos/$ex"
  npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 lint; echo "saída: $?"
done

abas.html:
◆  Linting a1-sorteio/index.html

  ✗ [~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-motion-v72/kit/exemplos/a1-sorteio/index.html:24:24] non_deterministic_code: Script contains `Math.random()` which produces non-deterministic output. Renders may differ between frames or runs.
    Fix: Use a seeded PRNG (e.g. a simple mulberry32) so renders are deterministic across frames.

◇  1 error(s), 0 warning(s)
saída: 1
◆  Linting a1-semente/index.html

◇  0 errors, 0 warnings
saída: 0

The lint exits with code 1 when it finds an error: you can use it as a gate before any render.

secoes.sub: Test run, lint, and your seed.

exercicios.texto: Clone the course into ~/projetos and run the "two renders of each and the comparison" block.
exercicios.pronto: a1-sorteio ends with DIFEREM: 89 de 90 quadros and saída: 1; a1-semente with IGUAIS: 90/90 quadros and saída: 0. (On your computer the number of differing frames may vary; what can't happen is the seed giving a different result.)

exercicios.titulo: E2 · The lint as a gate
exercicios.pronto: a1-sorteio shows non_deterministic_code and saída: 1; a1-semente shows 0 errors, 0 warnings and saída: 0.

exercicios.texto: In /tmp/ensaio-motion/a1/a1-semente, replace mulberry32(42) with mulberry32(7), render twice (render-3.mp4 and render-4.mp4, using the same command from the block), and compare: 3 with 4, then 1 with 3.
exercicios.pronto: bash ~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-motion-v72/kit/comparar-quadros.sh render-3.mp4 render-4.mp4 → IGUAIS: 90/90 quadros; the same with render-1.mp4 render-3.mp4 → starts with DIFEREM:.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: Who decides which instant the composition draws?
opcoes: The render engine, which asks for an exact time on every frame.
The browser, drawing at whatever speed the machine can manage.
FFmpeg, which picks the frames when it assembles the MP4.
The graphics card, depending on the computer's load.
perguntas.explica: The engine asks for the moment (2.5 s, frame 75) and the composition draws that moment. That's why speed doesn't change the result: in the same environment, a slow machine takes longer, but gives the same frames.

perguntas.p: Two renders of the same composition came out with 89 of 90 frames different. What should you look for first?
opcoes: A different encoder between the two renders.
Math.random, Date.now, or a network fetch inside the composition.
Running out of memory on the second render.
A font that didn't load in time.
perguntas.explica: Randomness inside the composition is the most common cause, and the lint points to Math.random by line. Both renders used the same hyperframes@0.8.176 and the same FFmpeg: what changed was the input.

perguntas.p: What is a seeded random draw for?
opcoes: To make the render faster on a slow machine.
To make the lint stop complaining without changing anything in the result.
To make the variety repeat identically on every render.
To make each render come out as a new, different version.
perguntas.explica: The seed fixes the sequence of numbers: the points are still scattered, but always in the same places. Changing the seed changes the pattern on purpose, and again in a repeatable way.

perguntas.p: Why compare frame by frame and not the whole MP4?
opcoes: Because md5sum can't read large MP4 files.
Because comparing frames is much faster than reading the file.
Because FFmpeg can only hash frames, not files.
Because metadata changes the file even when the images are identical.
perguntas.explica: What matters is the image. framemd5 decodes each frame and compares the pixels; the hash of the whole file also changes with metadata that never shows on screen.

itens.texto: The video is a page that draws any instant the engine asks for.
Same input, same frames: that's what lets you fix one detail without redoing the rest.
Seeded draw, engine time, and data saved in the folder; the lint keeps watch.
